mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes GLE 350 or 450 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M276 engine for the GLE 350 costs £3,200-£4,000 supply-only; a rebuilt M256 engine for the GLE 450 costs £4,500-£7,000 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - the M256's 48V system requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes GLE 350?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the M276 V6 engine. If ignored, it can lead to misfires, cam/crank correlation codes, and catastrophic engine damage if the chain jumps a tooth.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLE 450 engine (M256) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M256 inline-six is considered robust and reliable, thanks to its simplified inline-six design with inherent mechanical balance. However, it has known 48V system issues that can immobilise the vehicle, as well as timing chain noise and carbon buildup on intake valves.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes GLE 350 and 450 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M276 V6 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000+ miles before major work. The M256 inline-six is too new for definitive long-term data, but with regular maintenance, similar longevity is expected.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes GLE 350 or 450?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the GLE is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt M276 costs £3,200-£4,000 - far less than replacing a £12,000-£22,000 vehicle. The GLE 450's higher value (£25,000-£45,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes GLE 350 or 450 petrol need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 or 229.51 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M276 requires approximately 7 litres; the M256 requires approximately 7.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz GLE Class 350/450 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The GLE 350 launched with the W166 generation in 2015, powered by the M276 DE35 3.5-litre naturally aspirated V6 - a smooth, refined engine producing 302hp. In 2019, the all-new W167 GLE 450 replaced it with the M256 3.0-litre inline-six turbocharged petrol featuring 48V EQ Boost mild-hybrid technology - more power, better efficiency, and a completely different driving character.

milestones.description: M276 DE35, 3.5L naturally aspirated V6, 302hp @ 6,500rpm (GLE 350, W166)
M256, 3.0L inline-six turbocharged with 48V EQ Boost, 367hp (GLE 450, W167)
Facelift W167; M256 continues with refinements to 48V system

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLE Class 350/450 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The GLE 350's M276 V6 and the GLE 450's M256 inline-six are both fundamentally refined petrol engines, but each has well-documented weaknesses that drive replacement decisions. The M276's timing chain and tensioner wear is its Achilles' heel - a £1,000 specialist repair that can prevent a £4,000 replacement. The M256's 48V mild-hybrid system adds complexity that can leave owners stranded. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M276 Timing Chain & Tensioner Wear - The V6 Petrol's Critical Weak Point
problems.rootCause: The M276 V6 is generally durable and refined, with 200,000+ km examples common, but has well-documented timing chain and tensioner wear from neglected oil intervals. The plastic timing chain guides can become brittle with heat cycling, leading to rattle on cold start. If ignored, the chain can jump timing, causing piston-to-valve contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, camshaft sprockets

problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise on cold start from your GLE 350, act immediately. The M276's timing chain is accessible for tensioner and chain replacement, though guides typically require more extensive work. Specialist pricing of £1,000-£1,600 for a full chain kit is significantly lower than dealer rates. problems.h4: M276 Camshaft Magnet Oil Leaks & Thermostat Failure - Hidden Cost Traps
problems.rootCause: The M276 can suffer from camshaft magnet oil leaks, causing oil to seep into wiring harnesses and potentially causing misfires. Thermostat failure (fault codes P0597-P0599) can cause the engine to run cold, reducing efficiency and triggering warning lights.

repairOptions.longevity: If oil leak is caught early

problems.recommendation: Camshaft magnet oil leaks on the M276 are common but not usually urgent. If you notice oil around the camshaft magnets or experience misfires, have a specialist inspect the seals immediately. Thermostat failure is also common - if your GLE 350 takes longer than usual to warm up, budget £350-£550 for replacement.

problems.h4: M256 48V System Failure - The Inline-Six's Silent Killer
problems.rootCause: The M256's 48V integrated starter-generator (ISG) and lithium-ion battery are critical components of Mercedes' EQ Boost mild hybrid system. The 48V battery can fail internally, causing a complete no-start condition that cannot be jump-started. Coolant pump issues have also been reported, with erratic cooling and warning lights.

repairOptions.longevity: Check your VIN for outstanding recalls

problems.recommendation: If your GLE 450 displays a "48V battery malfunction" warning, do not assume a conventional jump start will work - the 48V system is entirely separate from the 12V starter battery.
